admission.justification: The current changed regression isolates the old strip-all-whitespace error. Regressing this guard could hide a joining/splitting edit, including must not into mustnot, as an innocuous whitespace-only result during future wording review.

applicability: textDiff classification of two supplied JavaScript strings.
conditions: Exact strings are identical; unequal strings need equal ordered non-whitespace token arrays for whitespace_only.
Non-whitespace runs retain punctuation; joining or splitting such runs changes that array and reaches words.
exclusions: Natural-language truth, locale-aware word/grapheme segmentation, original-file byte-decoding preservation, generated semantic effects and fresh runtime acceptance.

evidence: dashboard/src/panels/review/wordDiff.test.ts::decides by bytes: identical, whitespace only, or words
Compared actual BASE/current token predicate, caller and assertion phases; no equivalent current stored word-diff invariant found. This is a source-bound proof, not a new test run.

statement: A changed supplied text is whitespace-only only when its ordered non-whitespace tokens are equal; joining or splitting a word is a word change, not hidden by stripping all whitespace.
